lessons.title: Kandinsky Circles
lessons.summary: Students create concentric circles inspired by Wassily Kandinsky while exploring warm and cool colors.
steps: Show "Squares with Concentric Circles" and talk about colors.
Fold paper into 4 squares.
Draw circles inside circles in each square with oil pastels.
Paint over them with watercolors (the pastel resists!).
Assemble everyone's work into a class quilt.
lessons.notes: Makes a stunning bulletin board.

lessons.title: Eric Carle Painted Paper Collage
lessons.summary: Students paint textured papers, then cut them up to build an animal collage just like Eric Carle.
steps: Read an Eric Carle book and look closely at the illustrations.
Day 1: Paint papers and add texture with tools.
Day 2: Cut shapes from the painted papers.
Assemble an animal on background paper.
Write: "___, ___, what do you see?"
lessons.notes: Spread over two days so the papers can dry.

lessons.title: Symmetry Butterflies
lessons.summary: Fold-and-blot painting makes beautifully symmetrical butterflies.
steps: Talk about symmetry in nature.
Drop paint on one side of the fold.
Fold, press, and open to reveal the match.
When dry, add a pipe-cleaner body.
Hang them in the windows.
lessons.notes: Ties nicely to a life cycle science unit.

lessons.title: Salt Watercolor Snowflakes
lessons.summary: Draw snowflakes with glue, sprinkle salt, and touch on watercolor — the color spreads like magic.
steps: Look at real snowflake photos — six points!
Draw a snowflake with glue.
Cover it with salt and shake off the extra.
Gently touch watercolor to the salt and watch it travel.
Dry flat overnight.
lessons.notes: Use trays to catch the salt. Drip slowly for the best effect.

lessons.title: Fall Leaf Rubbings
lessons.summary: Students collect leaves and make crayon rubbings to reveal veins, edges, and shapes.
steps: Go on a leaf walk around the playground.
Place a leaf vein-side up under the paper.
Rub with the side of a peeled crayon.
Layer more leaves in different colors.
Label the leaf parts (stem, veins, edge).
lessons.notes: Use fresh leaves — dry ones crumble.

lessons.title: Mirror Self-Portraits
lessons.summary: Students study their faces in a mirror and draw detailed self-portraits.
steps: Show a few self-portraits by famous artists.
Look in mirrors: notice the shapes of eyes, nose, and hair.
Draw lightly in pencil, then add color.
Add a background showing something you love.
Display as "Our Class Family."
lessons.notes: Repeat at the end of the year to see how much they have grown!

lessons.title: All About Me Bag
lessons.summary: Students bring three items in a paper bag that tell about themselves, then share with the class.
steps: Model by sharing your own bag.
Send bags home with a note.
Each day, 3–4 students share their items.
Classmates ask one question each.
Graph the things you have in common.
lessons.notes: Builds community during the first weeks.

lessons.title: Build-a-Monster Adjectives
lessons.summary: Students create friendly monsters and describe them using adjectives.
steps: Read "Go Away, Big Green Monster!"
Brainstorm describing words together.
Build a monster.
Write three sentences with adjectives.
Classmates guess which monster is being described.
lessons.notes: Friendly monsters, not scary ones!

lessons.title: Gratitude Turkey
lessons.summary: Students write what they are thankful for on feathers to build a class turkey.
steps: Talk about gratitude.
Students write one thank-you on each feather.
Add the feathers to the class turkey.
Share in a circle.
Send home a mini version for families.
lessons.notes: Display in the hallway all November.

lessons.title: Gingerbread Man Hunt
lessons.summary: After reading The Gingerbread Man, the class follows clues around school to find him.
steps: Read the story together.
Discover the gingerbread man has run away!
Follow clues to the office, library, and gym.
Find him back in class with cookies.
Write a retell of the adventure.
lessons.notes: Let other staff in on the fun. Great for learning school locations.

lessons.title: Conversation Heart Graphing
lessons.summary: Sort, graph, and compare candy hearts by color.
steps: Estimate how many hearts are in your bag.
Sort them by color.
Make a bar graph.
Answer: Most? Least? How many more?
Read the messages for fun.
lessons.notes: Check for allergies; paper hearts work as an alternative.

lessons.title: When I'm 100 Years Old
lessons.summary: Students imagine life at 100 years old and write and draw about it.
steps: Talk about what life might be like at 100.
Brainstorm ideas together.
Write: "When I am 100, I will…"
Draw yourself at 100.
Share with the class.
lessons.notes: Always a huge hit!

lessons.title: Leprechaun Trap STEM
lessons.summary: Teams design and build a leprechaun trap from recyclables.
steps: Read a leprechaun story.
Plan a trap.
Build with a partner.
Test it out.
Next morning, find tiny footprints!
lessons.notes: Mid-March fun. Tiny green footprints sell the magic.

lessons.title: Sight Word Swat
lessons.summary: Two players race to swat the sight word that is called — quick, active practice with high-frequency words.
materials: Sight word cards (or words written on the board)
steps: Post 10–15 sight words on the board.
Two students stand ready with swatters.
Say a word (or use it in a sentence). The first to swat it reads it aloud for a point.
Rotate players quickly so everyone gets a turn.
Finish by reading all the words together chorally.
lessons.notes: A great 5-minute warm-up. For small group, play on the table with word cards.

lessons.title: Roll & Read Word Families
lessons.summary: Students roll a die and read a CVC word from that column, building decoding speed with word families.
steps: Model blending sounds: /c/ /a/ /t/ — cat!
A partner rolls the die and reads a word from the matching column.
If read correctly, they highlight it.
Keep playing until one column is completely highlighted.
Challenge: write a silly sentence using two of the words.
lessons.notes: Easy to differentiate — swap in blends, digraphs, or silent-e words.

lessons.title: Story Map Sticky Notes
lessons.summary: After a read-aloud, students retell the story by placing sticky notes under Beginning, Middle, and End.
materials: Chart paper with B / M / E columns
steps: Read the book aloud, stopping to predict.
Turn and talk: What happened first? Next? At the end?
Each student draws or writes one event on a sticky note.
Place the notes in the right column and retell the story together.
Add the characters and setting at the top.
lessons.notes: Supports RL.1.2 and RL.1.3. Follow up by letting students make their own mini-book retell.

lessons.title: Sound Boxes
lessons.summary: Students push a counter into a box for each sound they hear — powerful phonemic awareness and spelling practice.
steps: Say a word slowly: "ship."
Students repeat it and push one counter per sound: /sh/ /i/ /p/.
Count it up: 3 sounds, but 4 letters!
Replace the counters with letters.
Read the word back together.
lessons.notes: Keep it short (5–8 minutes). Fantastic for intervention groups.

lessons.title: How to Build a Snowman
lessons.summary: Sequencing writing with First, Next, Then, and Last — students write a how-to for building a snowman.
steps: Read a snowman book and talk about the steps.
Put the picture cards in order as a class.
Model a sentence for each transition word.
Students write and illustrate each step on their flaps.
Share with a partner and act out the steps.
lessons.notes: Swap the topic by season: How to Carve a Pumpkin, How to Plant a Seed, How to Make a Valentine.

lessons.title: Valentine Kindness Letters
lessons.summary: Students learn the parts of a friendly letter and write a kind valentine to a classmate or school helper.
steps: Introduce the parts: date, greeting, body, closing, signature.
Brainstorm kind words and compliments together.
Draw names so everyone receives a letter.
Write and decorate the letters.
Deliver them to mailboxes on Valentine's Day.
lessons.notes: Include the custodian, cafeteria staff, and nurse for a schoolwide smile.

lessons.title: Number Line Hop
lessons.summary: Kids become the counters! Students hop forward and back on a giant floor number line to act out addition and subtraction stories within 20.
steps: Tape a long line on the floor and lay number cards 0–20 in order.
Read a story problem: "Sam had 7 stickers and got 4 more."
A student stands on 7 and hops forward 4 while the class counts on aloud: "8, 9, 10, 11!"
Everyone writes the matching number sentence (7 + 4 = 11) on whiteboards.
Switch to "take away" stories and hop backward.
Let students invent their own story problems for a friend to hop.
lessons.notes: Perfect for wiggly days. Extend by hopping by 2s, or by starting on the bigger number to practice counting on (1.OA.C.5).

lessons.title: Make 10 Go Fish
lessons.summary: A twist on Go Fish where partners hunt for two cards that make ten — great for building fluency with ten-facts.
steps: Model with a ten-frame: "I have 6. How many more do I need to make 10?"
Deal 5 cards to each player and spread the rest face-down as the "pond."
On your turn, ask a partner for the card that makes 10 with one in your hand: "Do you have a 4?"
If they don't, they say "Go fish!" and you draw.
Lay down each pair and say the fact aloud: "6 + 4 = 10!"
The player with the most pairs when the pond is empty wins.
lessons.notes: Leave ten-frames out for friends who still need the visual. Works great as a math center once modeled (1.OA.C.6).

lessons.title: Paper Clip Measuring
lessons.summary: How long is it? Students measure classroom objects with paper clips to learn non-standard measurement — no gaps and no overlaps!
materials: Jumbo paper clips (some linked into chains)
Objects to measure: pencil, glue stick, crayon box, book, shoe
steps: Show a pencil measured the wrong way (with gaps and overlaps). Ask: "What went wrong?"
Model lining up clips end-to-end starting at the very edge.
Partners estimate first, then measure 5 objects and record.
Put the objects in order from shortest to longest.
Share: "Did anything measure exactly the same?"
lessons.notes: Next day, measure the same objects with cubes and talk about why the numbers changed (1.MD.A.2).

lessons.title: 100 Things Collections
lessons.summary: Families send in 100 small objects; students sort them into groups of ten and count by tens to 100.
materials: Zip bags with a family note
steps: A week ahead, send home a note asking for 100 small items (cereal, buttons, pom-poms, LEGO).
On 100th Day, students sort their items into 10 groups of 10.
Count together by tens: 10, 20, 30… 100!
Double-check by coloring a hundreds chart while counting by ones.
Do a gallery walk: why do some collections look bigger even though they are all 100?
lessons.notes: Keep a few extra collections ready for anyone who forgets.

lessons.title: Pumpkin Investigation
lessons.summary: A hands-on pumpkin day: estimate, measure, test sink or float, and count the seeds by tens.
steps: Estimate how big around the pumpkin is by cutting a piece of yarn. Wrap it around to check who was close!
Weigh the pumpkin and compare it to classroom objects.
Predict: sink or float? Test it in the tub (it floats!).
Scoop the seeds and count them by putting 10 in each cup.
Write one sentence about something surprising.
lessons.notes: Messy but memorable! Cut the tops off ahead of time. Pumpkins float because they are hollow inside.

lessons.title: Shape Monster Builders
lessons.summary: Students compose new shapes with pattern blocks, then design a friendly "shape monster" and count its sides and corners.
steps: Review shape names, sides, and vertices (corners).
Challenge: build a hexagon out of other blocks. How many ways can you find?
Students glue paper shapes together to build a monster.
Fill in: "My monster has __ triangles and __ squares."
Partners count the total number of sides on each other's monsters.
lessons.notes: Covers 1.G.A.1–2. Hallway display idea: "Shape Monsters Ate Our Hallway!"

lessons.title: Feelings Freeze Dance
lessons.summary: Dance when the music plays; when it stops, freeze in the shape of the feeling on the card.
materials: Feelings cards (happy, sad, mad, surprised, scared)
steps: Review the feelings and what our faces and bodies look like for each.
Play music while students dance.
Stop the music and hold up a feelings card.
Students freeze showing that feeling.
Ask: "When have you felt that way?"
lessons.notes: A brain break and SEL lesson in one.

lessons.title: Rhythm Names
lessons.summary: Clap the syllables in names, then read simple rhythm notation with "ta" and "ti-ti."
steps: Clap each student's name.
Introduce "ta" (one sound on a beat) and "ti-ti" (two sounds on a beat).
Match names to rhythm cards.
Play the rhythms with sticks.
Students compose their own 4-beat rhythm.
lessons.notes: Builds phonological awareness too!

lessons.title: Skip-Count Workout
lessons.summary: Count by 2s, 5s, and 10s while doing exercises — math and movement together.
steps: Choose a number to count by.
Pick an exercise (jumping jacks, squats, arm circles).
Count aloud with every move up to 100.
Switch exercises and numbers.
Cool down by counting backward slowly.
lessons.notes: Skip-counting songs on YouTube add variety.

lessons.title: Animal Moves Dice
lessons.summary: Roll a giant die to pick an animal movement — perfect for brain breaks and indoor recess.
materials: Large foam die or cube with animal pictures
steps: Make the die: frog jump, bear crawl, crab walk, flamingo stand, snake slither, kangaroo hop.
Roll the die.
Everyone moves like that animal for 20 seconds.
Roll again!
End with a slow "sloth" breathing stretch.
lessons.notes: Swap in seasonal animals (penguin waddle in winter!).

lessons.title: Shaker Eggs & Steady Beat
lessons.summary: Students make shakers and use them to keep a steady beat with songs.
steps: Fill eggs with rice or beans and seal them with tape.
Compare the sounds of different fillings.
Practice a steady beat with a favorite song.
Play loud/soft and fast/slow.
Form a class band!
lessons.notes: Tape the eggs very well!

lessons.title: Parachute Patterns
lessons.summary: Use a play parachute to make AB and ABC movement patterns.
steps: Everyone holds a handle.
Make small waves and big waves.
Create a pattern: up-down-up-down (AB).
Add more: up-down-shake (ABC).
Pop balls off the top!
lessons.notes: Best in the gym or outside. Ties to pattern work in math.

lessons.title: Sink or Float?
lessons.summary: Students predict, test, and sort everyday objects that sink or float.
materials: Objects: cork, penny, crayon, foil, sponge, apple, rock, plastic spoon
steps: Show each object. Students predict with a thumbs up (float) or down (sink).
Test one at a time and record on the T-chart.
Ask: What do the floaters have in common?
Challenge: Can you make the foil float? Can you make it sink?
Draw one surprising result in science journals.
lessons.notes: Lay towels down! A foil-boat "how many pennies?" challenge makes a great follow-up.

lessons.title: Seed in a Bag Greenhouse
lessons.summary: Students sprout a bean in a zip bag taped to the window and observe it grow day by day.
steps: Wet a paper towel and fold it into the bag.
Place 2–3 beans in the middle and seal it.
Tape the bags to a sunny window with names on them.
Observe each day and draw roots, shoots, and leaves.
After a week, measure growth with cubes.
lessons.notes: Beans usually sprout in 3–5 days. Mist if the towel dries out.

lessons.title: Five Senses Popcorn
lessons.summary: Explore all five senses with popcorn — see it, hear it pop, smell it, touch it, and taste it!
steps: Introduce the five senses with an anchor chart.
Look at and touch unpopped kernels. Describe them.
Pop the popcorn — listen and smell!
Taste and describe it with adjectives.
Complete the five-senses sheet.
lessons.notes: Check for allergies first. Pair with a "popcorn words" adjective chart.

lessons.title: Melting Ice Race
lessons.summary: Where will ice melt fastest? Students predict and test ice cubes in different spots around school.
steps: Ask: What makes ice melt?
Choose 4 spots: sunny window, shady corner, desk, and in a zip bag held in hands.
Predict which cube will melt first.
Check every 10 minutes and record.
Discuss heat and compare results to predictions.
lessons.notes: Add a cube sprinkled with salt for a bonus investigation.

lessons.title: Shadow Tracing
lessons.summary: Students trace a partner's shadow with chalk in the morning and afternoon to see how the sun "moves."
steps: Model shadows indoors with a flashlight and a toy.
Outside in the morning, trace partner shadows and mark where their feet were.
Return after lunch, stand in the same spot, and trace again.
Compare: What changed? Why?
Record observations and draw both shadows.
lessons.notes: Connects to 1-ESS1-1 (patterns of the sun). Check the forecast for a sunny day!

lessons.title: Good Vibrations
lessons.summary: Students discover that sound is made by vibrations using rubber bands, drums, and dancing rice.
steps: Hum with a hand on your throat — what do you feel?
Stretch rubber bands over a box and pluck them.
Sprinkle rice on the plastic-wrap drum and tap nearby — watch it bounce!
Compare loud taps and soft taps.
Finish the sentence: "Sound is made when…"
lessons.notes: Matches 1-PS4-1. The rice dance is always a hit.

lessons.title: Morning Meeting Greeting Circle
lessons.summary: Start the day with a greeting, a share, a quick group activity, and the morning message.
steps: Gather in a circle.
Greeting: handshake, wave, or elbow bump.
Share: one or two students share something.
Group activity: a quick game or song.
Read the morning message together.
lessons.notes: 15–20 minutes daily; it pays off all year.

lessons.title: Calm-Down Corner
lessons.summary: Set up a cozy space with tools for big feelings and teach breathing strategies.
materials: Breathing cards (smell the flower, blow out the candle)
steps: Introduce the corner as a place to help, not a punishment.
Teach each tool, one at a time.
Practice breathing strategies together.
Role-play when to use it.
Check in with students afterward.
lessons.notes: Model using it yourself!

lessons.title: Bucket Filling
lessons.summary: Students learn to fill each other's buckets with kindness.
steps: Read the book.
Discuss bucket fillers and bucket dippers.
Each student gets a bucket.
Write or draw kind notes to fill each other's buckets.
Reflect at the end of the week.
lessons.notes: An ongoing routine all year long.

lessons.title: Attention Getters
lessons.summary: A collection of fun call-and-response attention getters.
steps: Teach one at a time: "Class, class!" — "Yes, yes!"
"Hocus pocus!" — "Everybody focus!"
"Macaroni and cheese!" — "Everybody freeze!"
"1, 2, 3, eyes on me!" — "1, 2, eyes on you!"
Practice until automatic.
lessons.notes: Rotate them to keep things fresh.

lessons.title: Classroom Jobs Chart
lessons.summary: Give every student a job to build responsibility and ownership.
steps: Brainstorm classroom jobs together.
Explain each job.
Assign jobs and rotate them weekly.
Check in on how jobs went.
Celebrate a job well done.
lessons.notes: Ideas: line leader, door holder, plant waterer, librarian, messenger.

lessons.title: Feelings Check-In
lessons.summary: Students check in each morning by moving their name to a feelings chart.
materials: Feelings chart with zones or emojis
steps: Teach feelings vocabulary.
Each morning, students clip their name on a feeling.
Quietly check in with anyone who needs it.
Discuss strategies for each feeling.
Notice patterns over time.
lessons.notes: Make it part of the arrival routine.

lessons.title: Me on the Map
lessons.summary: Students make nested circles that show where they live: me → home → street → town → state → country → world.
steps: Zoom out from the school on Google Earth or a map.
Talk about each level: home, street, town, state, country, continent.
Students label and decorate each circle.
Stack and glue them largest to smallest.
Share: "I live in ___, which is in ___."
lessons.notes: Send a note home so families can help students learn their address.

lessons.title: Community Helpers Interview
lessons.summary: Students learn about jobs in their community and interview a real community helper.
steps: Sort helper cards by what they do (keep us safe, keep us healthy, help us learn).
Brainstorm interview questions as a class.
Invite a guest (nurse, firefighter, parent) to answer questions.
Students draw and write about a job they might like.
Bind the pages into a class book: "When I Grow Up."
lessons.notes: Ask families ahead of time — many love to visit!

lessons.title: Then and Now: School Long Ago
lessons.summary: Students compare photos of schools long ago with school today using a T-chart.
materials: Picture sort cards (slate, chalkboard, tablet, pencil)
steps: Show a one-room schoolhouse photo. What do you notice? What do you wonder?
Compare it with a photo of your classroom.
Sort picture cards into Then and Now.
Write: "Long ago, kids ___. Today we ___."
Discuss: What is still the same?
lessons.notes: Invite a grandparent to share school memories.

lessons.title: Our Class Promise
lessons.summary: Students create and sign a class promise, learning why rules help a community work together.
steps: Read a story about rules.
Discuss: Why do families, schools, and towns need rules?
Brainstorm promises as positive statements ("We use kind words").
Vote on 4–5 promises.
Everyone signs or adds a handprint.
lessons.notes: Refer back to it all year. Pairs well with the SEL section.

lessons.title: Family Traditions Graph
lessons.summary: Students share family traditions and build a class graph showing how families celebrate.
steps: Send home a short survey about a favorite family tradition.
Students share their tradition in a circle.
Group similar traditions and graph them with sticky notes.
Discuss what is the same and different.
Make a class book of traditions.
lessons.notes: Keep it inclusive — every tradition counts (even pancake Saturdays!).

lessons.title: Needs vs. Wants Shop
lessons.summary: Students sort pictures into needs and wants, then "shop" with a pretend budget.
materials: Small items for a pretend store
steps: Define needs (food, water, shelter, clothing) and wants.
Sort picture cards together.
Give each student $10 to shop.
They must buy a need first, then a want if money remains.
Reflect: Was it hard to choose?
lessons.notes: A gentle introduction to economics: choices and scarcity.
